issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem specification and the solution expect addGuestStudents(int). This parameter mismatch prevents students from implementing the method with the expected single-argument signature and will cause confusion or test failures because the template does not provide the method signature required by the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. Alternatively, provide an overloaded version that accepts (int) and delegate to a private implementation if validation is required, ensuring the public API matches the problem statement and solution.

issues.description: Method signature for the same conceptual operation 'addGuestStudents' is inconsistent: the problem statement (and the solution implementation) specify addGuestStudents(int), but the template provides addGuestStudents(int, boolean). This mismatch creates a clear mapping barrier — students reading the exercise expect to implement/complete a single-parameter method, but the starter code has a different signature (extra boolean). It can cause compile/test failures and unnecessary confusion about the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } — remove the extra boolean parameter (or provide an overloaded one but keep the single-parameter version present) so students can clearly map the requirement to the starter code.
